newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strike to cut number of French flights on Nov 27-28.
newsitem.headline: Strike to cut number of French flights on Nov 27-28.

text.p: Most French airlines predicted wide disruption on Wednesday and Thursday from a strike by pilots, engineers and stewards protesting at restructurings and feared job cuts.
Air France said it would guarantee two-thirds of its long-haul flights and a quarter of its medium-haul flights over the two days.

Air France Europe, the short-haul unit of Air France, said it expected to cut more than half its flights. It said it would guarantee 213 flights on Wednesday and 200 on Thursday, against 480 normally.
The unions reaffirmed their strike calls on Tuesday despite some signs of hope from talks with Transport Minister Bernard Pons on Monday.
A union statement said they had "noted some progress, notably in terms of reducing distortions of competition. Nevertheless, nothing allows us to withdraw the strike call".
The strikes, first called almost two weeks ago, will add to transport problems in France, grappling with a nine-day old truckers stoppage paralysing many French roads.
Private airline AOM, owned by the state-backed CDR holding company, predicted it would maintain all its flights, both on domestic and international flights.
Air Liberte also predicted that its flights would be unaffected.
